name: pagination
summary: The compact pager under a table: an optional rows-per-page picker, "Page X of Y" and previous and next buttons.
useWhen: A table or list has more rows than fit comfortably, such as a credit history or a render queue, and people step through it a page at a time.

alternatives.name: A Load more button
alternatives.when: people browse a feed of pictures rather than look up rows, as in the media grid

alternatives.name: tabs
alternatives.when: the pages are named views, not slices of one list

rules.do: Show the current page and the total, "Page 2 of 7", between the previous and next buttons.
rules.dont: Show bare arrows with no page count, so people cannot tell how far the list goes.

rules.do: Go back to page 1 when the rows per page or a filter changes.
rules.dont: Keep the old page number, which can point past the end of the shorter list.

rules.do: Place the pager directly under the rows it pages, aligned to the table's width.
rules.dont: Float it far from the table or repeat it above and below a short list.

a11y: Renders a `nav` landmark; name it for what it pages with `aria-label`, such as "Usage history pages".
The previous and next buttons are named and disable at the first and last page.
The page line is a polite live region, so screen readers announce the new page after each step.
The rows picker is labelled by its visible "Rows" text.
